item.title: China establishes data-focused new central SOE to unlock data value
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-21
XIONGAN, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- China National Data Group Co., Ltd., a new state-owned enterprise (SOE) directly administered by the central government, was officially inaugurated at a ceremony in Xiongan New Area, north China's Hebei Province, on Tuesday.
Headquartered in Xiongan New Area, the newly established enterprise is tasked with specializing in the development and utilization of data resources, bringing the total number of SOEs directly administered by the central government to 100.
It is positioned as a national team for data services, a leader in data infrastructure connectivity and a strategic force for national data sci-tech innovation.
The group said it will provide clients with inclusive and secure data services, and industry data governance services.
Focusing on advancing China's "AI Plus" initiative, the group also vowed to provide high-quality datasets and corpora to further the development of the AI industry.
The establishment of the new central SOE comes as data has increasingly become a new type of production factor driving China's digital and intelligent transformation.
Unlike traditional production factors, unprocessed data can hardly generate value. Only data that is connected to real scenarios, addresses practical difficulties and undergoes processing can be transformed into usable resources, analysts said.
China has been bolstering its efforts to develop a data market in recent years. In 2020, the country listed data as a new type of production factor, alongside traditional factors such as land, labor, capital and technology, highlighting its growing role in driving economic growth and digital transformation.
Following the introduction of a three-year action plan in 2024 to boost the development and application of data as a production factor, China has seen the value of data resources continue to be unleashed.
The plan sets out efforts to expand the breadth and depth of data applications across key sectors, foster new industries, business models and growth drivers, and unlock the multiplier effect of data in supporting high-quality development.
In 2025, China's total data output reached 52.26 zettabytes, up 27.28 percent year on year and accounting for about 27.44 percent of the global total, according to a national survey on data resources released in April this year. A zettabyte is the equivalent of about one trillion gigabytes.
Enterprises contributed about 90 percent of incremental data output, while emerging fields such as embodied intelligence and the low-altitude economy saw surging growth in data production, the survey noted.
Traditional sectors such as industrial manufacturing, transportation and logistics, and software and information technology services also posted marked expansion in data output.
To further unlock the potential of data resources, Chinese central authorities have pledged greater efforts to build an open, shared and secure nationally integrated data market, according to a set of guidelines aimed at accelerating the development of new quality productive forces.
Efforts will be made to promote the deep integration of the digital economy and the real economy, and optimize the layout, construction and operation of national data infrastructure, according to the guidelines, which were jointly issued by the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council earlier this month.
As massive amounts of data are scattered across different departments, industries and fields, China National Data Group is expected to overcome challenges including barriers to data circulation, high data governance costs and insufficient supply of high-quality datasets, analysts said.

item.title: Chinese premier eyes further alignment of development strategies with Tajikistan, higher-quality SCO development with all parties
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-21
DUSHANBE, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- During a packed three-day visit of high-level engagements in Dushanbe, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said China is willing to deeply align its development strategies with Tajikistan and advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, and work with all parties to promote higher-quality development of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO).
Li arrived here Sunday for an official visit and the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of Member States of the SCO in Tajikistan.
In his meeting with Tajik President Emomali Rahmon, Li said that China stands ready to broaden bilateral trade with Tajikistan, strengthen cooperation in infrastructure, green minerals, connectivity and other fields, and expand cooperation in emerging industries such as the digital economy and artificial intelligence to jointly build new drivers of economic growth.
China will import more high-quality goods from Tajikistan, encourage Chinese enterprises to invest and start businesses in Tajikistan, and hopes that Tajikistan will continue to provide a favorable business environment for enterprises, Li said during his talks with Tajik Prime Minister Kokhir Rasulzoda.
Both sides should expand exchanges and cooperation in areas such as culture, education, health, sports and local-level fields to enhance the sense of gain of the people of both countries, said Li, noting that the two countries should continue to deepen law enforcement and security cooperation to foster a stable and secure environment for personnel exchanges between the two sides.
This year, China begins the implementation of its 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), and Tajikistan is also advancing its National Development Strategy for the period up to 2030, Chinese President Xi Jinping said in his talks with Rahmon in May this year, adding that the two sides should focus on high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and further align their development strategies.
Now the two countries are seeking to enhance the alignment and cooperation across various fields to support the pursuit of their respective development goals.
Data show that China is Tajikistan's largest trading partner. In 2025, bilateral trade exceeded 30.8 billion yuan (about 4.5 billion U.S. dollars), up 12.5 percent year on year.
During Li's visit, the two sides witnessed the signing of multiple documents covering infrastructure development, education, anti-corruption and standardized cooperation.
Guzel Maitdinova, director of the Center for Geopolitical Studies at the Russian-Tajik (Slavonic) University, told Xinhua that the interaction between the two countries is gradually evolving into a multi-level system of cooperation -- encompassing political, economic, infrastructural, technological, and humanitarian spheres -- that is closely linked to the development of the SCO, China's Belt and Road Initiative, and broader regional processes in central Eurasia.
In his speech at the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of Member States of the SCO, Li said that all parties need to build greater consensus both on the level of underlying principles, including vision, philosophy and thinking, and the level of practical approaches, including operations and implementation, so as to shoulder its historic responsibility and take the initiative in steering the course of history.
Li said that the SCO should strengthen economic and trade cooperation and promote regional economic integration by leveraging the complementary strengths of its members, build a stable and resilient system of international transport corridors, and safeguard the stability and smooth functioning of global industrial and supply chains.
The SCO should also seek common interests amid differences in countries' concerns and work together to uphold world peace and stability, while promoting harmony and coexistence amid cultural differences, he added.
This year marks the 25th anniversary of the founding of the SCO. Over the past 25 years, it has shown that countries with different political systems, development paths and civilizations can pursue cooperation together.
"The SCO's international significance is therefore determined not only by its geographical reach or the combined potential of its member states, but also by its ability to translate political agreements into functioning mechanisms for security, economic cooperation, and diplomatic coordination," said Maitdinova.
Amid profound changes in the international landscape, the international role of the SCO is acquiring new dimensions. The organization is becoming not only a platform for regional dialogue and security coordination, but also a mechanism for reconciling the interests of states within an emerging multipolar world order, the expert added.
China stands ready to work hand in hand with all member states to enhance the organization's operational efficiency, strengthen and consolidate cooperation projects, and play a leading and exemplary role in advancing the SCO's high-quality development, implementing the four global initiatives proposed by President Xi, and building a community with a shared future for humanity, Li said.
China is ready to work with all parties to strengthen coordination and complete, as soon as possible, the institutional frameworks and rules for the four security centers, said Li, noting that China is also willing to sponsor 1,000 medical professionals from SCO countries to come to China for further training.
China, as one of the founding members of the SCO, has consistently expanded the organization's cooperation agenda and contributed to its development, SCO Deputy Secretary-General Ahmad Saidmurodzoda said in an earlier interview with Xinhua.

item.title: Chinese premier says to promote deeper, more substantive, more resilient cooperation with Russia
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-21
Chinese Premier Li Qiang arrives in St. Petersburg, Russia, Oct. 20, 2026. Li arrived here at the invitation of Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin to attend the 31st regular meeting between Chinese and Russian heads of government. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen)
ST. PETERSBURG, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- China is ready to work with Russia to make sustained efforts to steer bilateral cooperation in a direction that is deeper, more substantive and more resilient, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said Tuesday upon his arrival in St. Petersburg.
Both sides will push the China-Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for the new era to yield new and fruitful results, he added.
The premier said this year marks the 30th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Russia strategic partnership of coordination and the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation.
Looking back on the journey China and Russia have taken together, the two countries have jointly explored a way of getting along featuring non-alliance, non-confrontation and not targeting any third party, continuously deepened cooperation in various fields, and set a fine example of major-country relations featuring permanent good-neighborly friendship, comprehensive strategic coordination and mutually beneficial cooperation, Li said.
In particular, under the strategic guidance of Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in recent years, China-Russia relations have become more mature and resilient, with the foundation of political mutual trust growing ever stronger, mutually beneficial cooperation becoming increasingly solid, and the bonds of friendship from generation to generation growing ever closer, he said.
Noting that changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world, Li said the two heads of state have met twice this year, drawing a new blueprint for the development of bilateral relations.
The efforts made by both sides will bring greater benefits to the two peoples and inject valuable stability and certainty into world peace and development, he added.
Li arrived here after concluding an official visit to Tajikistan and attending the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of Member States of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization.

item.title: Chinese premier says SCO should promote regional stability, prosperity, contribute to global development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-21
Chinese Premier Li Qiang attends the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of Member States of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, Oct. 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Shen Hong)
DUSHANBE, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) should strive to promote regional stability and prosperity while contributing to common development worldwide, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said here on Tuesday.
Li made the remarks while addressing the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of Member States of the SCO in Tajikistan's capital of Dushanbe.
Noting that this year marks the 25th anniversary of the founding of the SCO, Li said the Bishkek summit held in September achieved a series of important outcomes, injecting fresh impetus into the promotion of peace and development.
Meanwhile, factors contributing to global instability and uncertainty continue to increase, he added.
He noted that at the Bishkek summit, Chinese President Xi Jinping pointed out that at the crossroads concerning the future of humanity, the SCO should shoulder its historic responsibility and take the initiative in steering the course of history.
To achieve this, Li said, all parties need to build greater consensus both on the level of underlying principles, including vision, philosophy and thinking, and the level of practical approaches, including operations and implementation.
At the level of underlying principles, he emphasized the importance of having a clear understanding of several fundamental issues and the vision to discern broader trends.
At present, Li said, different schools of thought are interacting and competing on the international stage, but multipolarity and economic globalization remain the prevailing trends.
Li called for embracing a global perspective and a strong sense of responsibility for the world, saying that the SCO should continue to uphold the Shanghai Spirit.
He urged the SCO to demonstrate perseverance in pursuing long-term goals. Noting that SCO countries share a common aspiration to promote friendship, safeguard security and pursue development, Li said all parties should remain steadfast, strengthen solidarity and move forward with resolve.
At the level of practical approaches, the premier said all parties need to strengthen cooperation and pursue practical innovation.
China stands ready to work hand in hand with all member states to enhance the organization's operational efficiency, strengthen and consolidate cooperation projects, and play a leading and exemplary role in advancing the SCO's high-quality development, implementing the four global initiatives proposed by President Xi, and building a community with a shared future for humanity, Li said.
He said China is ready to work with all parties to strengthen coordination and complete, as soon as possible, the institutional frameworks and rules for the four security centers.
China is also willing to sponsor 1,000 medical professionals from SCO countries to come to China for further training, continuously enhancing the well-being of people across the region, the premier said.
In recent years, the international community has seen growing calls to strengthen multilateralism and reform and improve global governance, Li said, noting that the SCO should strive to unite more international partners and play an active role at the global level.
To this end, he noted, it is particularly important to seek common ground while reserving differences and to build consensus while resolving differences.
The SCO should strengthen economic and trade cooperation and promote regional economic integration by leveraging the complementary strengths of its members, build a stable and resilient system of international transport corridors, and safeguard the stability and smooth functioning of global industrial and supply chains, Li said.
The SCO should also seek common interests amid differences in countries' concerns and work together to uphold world peace and stability, while promoting harmony and coexistence amid cultural differences, Li added.
Participants said the SCO has grown steadily and gained increasing international influence since its establishment 25 years ago.
They called for efforts to implement the outcomes of the Tianjin summit and Bishkek summit, further carry forward the "Shanghai Spirit," strengthen communication and coordination, promote the SCO's high-quality development and make greater contributions to regional and global peace and development.
After the meeting, Li and other participating leaders of SCO member states signed and issued a joint communique and approved cooperation documents covering trade and investment, industry and connectivity, as well as resolutions concerning the SCO's development.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang attends the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of Member States of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, Oct. 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen)

item.title: China's top economic planner vows more efforts to expand domestic demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-21
An aerial drone photo taken on Oct. 2, 2026 shows people visiting a night market in Wuzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. (Photo by He Huawen/Xinhua)
BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- China's top economic planner said Tuesday it will work with relevant departments to expand domestic demand with greater force and more effective measures in an effort to consolidate the foundation and momentum for steady economic recovery.
The National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) revealed this at a press conference on Tuesday following the release of the latest economic data on Monday, which showed the world's second-largest economy pressed ahead against pressures with a 4.6-percent economic growth in the first three quarters of 2026.
Commenting on the economic performance, NDRC official Zuo Gang said the economy, in the face of intensifying global geopolitical conflicts and frequent natural disasters, has demonstrated strong resilience and vitality with new growth drivers and improved structure.
Due to challenges such as the deepening impact of external shocks, an imbalance of strong supply and weak demand at home, and pronounced sectoral divergence, further measures will be taken to rev up the economy, according to the official.
"The NDRC will work with relevant departments to promptly introduce and implement incremental policies and promote synergy between existing and incremental policies with a view to achieving a good start for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030)," Zuo said.
China has targeted 2026 growth at 4.5 to 5 percent and will strive for better in practice.
BOOSTING CONSUMPTION
More efforts will be made to vigorously boost consumption, Zuo said.
Authorities will raise the share of public service spending in fiscal expenditure, strengthen inclusive policies that reach consumers directly, and promote the expansion and upgrading of goods consumption, including new energy vehicles and smart products, Zuo said.
The push comes as consumption shows signs of steady improvement. Total retail sales of goods and services rose 2.6 percent year-on-year in the first three quarters of 2026, with retail sales of services growing faster than goods and new forms of consumption continuing to emerge, official data showed. Final consumption expenditure contributed more to overall economic growth in the January-September period.
Chinese authorities have recently introduced a raft of measures aimed at boosting domestic demand, including offering interest subsidies for the housing loans of eligible homebuyers to help reduce home-buying costs and better unlock housing demand.
Through ultra-long special treasury bond issuance, 250 billion yuan (about 37.2 billion U.S. dollars) has been raised to support consumer goods trade-in programs, and 200 billion yuan to support large-scale equipment upgrades this year. Furthermore, 50 billion yuan was earmarked for the establishment of a special fiscal-financial coordination fund to boost domestic demand.
In addition to measures already announced, including lowering interest rate for pledged supplementary lending and increasing relending quotas to support sci-tech innovation and technological upgrades, "we will introduce new incremental policies in a timely manner as needed to ensure that the economy operates within an appropriate range," Zuo said.
PROMOTING INVESTMENT
Zuo said China will invest in both physical assets and human capital to expand effective investment.
Specifically, the NDRC will push for the implementation of the 109 major projects outlined in the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) and the "six networks" initiative, covering water, power, computing, communications, urban underground pipelines and logistics networks, Zuo said.
Ultra-long special treasury bond funds will be deployed more effectively, and the new policy-based financial instruments will be used at a faster pace, Zuo said, also vowing stronger support for social welfare, technology innovation, industrial upgrading and security resilience.
Zuo revealed plans to energize private investment by introducing private capital into major nuclear power, hydropower, and water conservancy projects. He also identified the optimization of computing power facility layouts and the renovation and upgrading of aging reservoirs as additional investment priorities.
China's investment is undergoing a profound shift in emphasis from traditional sectors to emerging ones, analysts said, noting that artificial intelligence and new infrastructure will serve as key engines for the next round of effective investment.
Official data showed the country's investment in innovation-driven sectors held up well in the first three quarters of 2026, even as overall fixed-asset investment continued to contract. Investment in intellectual property products rose 9.3 percent year-on-year in the January-September period, while investment in high-tech industries grew 4.9 percent.
Investment will increasingly serve the development of new quality productive forces and the building of a modern industrial system, with the ultimate results felt in expanded employment, rising incomes and improved living standards, said Liu Yuanchun, president of Shanghai University of Finance and Economics.

item.title: China's Q3 economy picks up pace, reinforcing role as global growth engine
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
* China's GDP grew 4.5 percent year on year in the third quarter, higher than the second quarter's reading of 4.3 percent, supported by fast-growing new drivers and fresh policy support.
* New growth drivers continued to expand, contributing more than 40 percent to China's economic growth in the first three quarters.
* More foreign firms are embracing "China Opportunity 2.0," deepening their integration into China's industrial and innovation chains.
An aerial drone photo taken on Sept. 18, 2026 shows a view of Tianjin Port in Tianjin, north China. (Xinhua/Sun Fanyue)
BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China's economy picked up pace in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026, supported by fast-growing new drivers and fresh policy support, staying on track to meet its annual growth target and remaining a leading engine of global growth.
China's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 4.5 percent year on year in Q3, higher than the second quarter's reading of 4.3 percent, data from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) showed Monday.
The world's second-largest economy generated about 107.11 trillion yuan (about 15.94 trillion U.S. dollars) in output during the January-September period, expanding 4.6 percent year on year, according to the NBS.
"The national economy forged ahead against pressure and continued to shift toward innovation-driven, high-quality development, with growing positive changes in major indicators," the NBS said in a statement.
China has consistently contributed around 30 percent of global economic growth, with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva saying in January that this contribution is expected to stay at roughly the same level in the coming years.
Tourists visit the Anshun ancient town in Anshun City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, Oct. 6, 2026. (Photo by Lu Wei/Xinhua)
GROWING RESILIENCE
Noting that the GDP growth of 4.6 percent in the first three quarters is in line with the country's annual growth target, NBS deputy head Mao Shengyong told a media conference that the economy added 5.7 trillion yuan in output during the period, the largest increase for the same period in the past five years.
In the third quarter, GDP growth picked up 0.2 percentage points from the second quarter, while some international institutions expected major economies to grow more slowly in July-September compared to the April-June period, Mao said.
There was also a notable rise in momentum on a monthly basis. In September, value-added industrial output rose 5.5 percent year on year, 0.3 percentage points faster than in August, while the services production index gained 4.8 percent, up 0.7 percentage points from the previous month.
Retail sales of consumer goods grew 1.1 percent in September, 0.7 percentage points faster than in August, and the surveyed urban unemployment rate edged down 0.1 percentage points from August to 5.2 percent.
"Growth momentum showed signs of marginal improvement in September," said Wen Bin, chief economist with China Minsheng Bank, citing faster industrial and services output, a rebound in consumption and an initial stabilization of investment.
China will step up efforts to expand domestic demand, improve supply, and make macro policies more effective to sustain the positive momentum of innovation-led and high-quality development, Mao said.
To this end, China has recently rolled out a batch of new policies, including financial and fiscal support. "With existing policies being implemented faster and incremental policies gradually taking effect, the economy is expected to continue improving in the fourth quarter," Wen said.
Humanoid robots are seen under training at an intelligent manufacturing plant for commercial vehicles of the Dongfeng Liuzhou Motor in Liuzhou City, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Jan. 30, 2026. (Photo by Zheng Changhao/Xinhua)
NEW DRIVERS AT WORK
New growth drivers continued to expand, contributing more than 40 percent to China's economic growth in the first three quarters. Value-added industrial output rose 5.3 percent year on year, with equipment manufacturing up 10.2 percent and high-tech manufacturing up 14.3 percent. Output of industrial robots, lithium-ion batteries and 3D printing equipment jumped 29.1 percent, 39.5 percent and 62.5 percent, respectively.
Monday's data also showed that the services sector expanded 5.2 percent year on year in the first three quarters, with information transmission, software and IT services up 10.4 percent, and leasing and business services up 12.3 percent.
The shift is visible in the economic structure. Manufacturing accounted for 25.7 percent of GDP in the first three quarters, up 0.6 percentage points from a year earlier, while the share of high-tech manufacturing in the value-added output of major industrial enterprises rose 1.6 percentage points. Investment in intellectual property products climbed 9.3 percent.
Traditional industries are also moving up the value chain. In Jingdezhen, a ceramics hub in east China's Jiangxi Province, local producers have embraced 3D printing in pottery making, propelling the sector's output to over 100 billion yuan. Meanwhile, some coal mining companies have implemented smart monitoring systems for underground operations, increasing efficiency by 30 percent.
Green development is creating openings as well. The penetration rate of new energy vehicles in China has stayed above 60 percent for six consecutive months, while the country's energy consumption per unit of GDP fell 3.1 percent in the first three quarters.
"The foundations of the economy remain solid, while new quality productive forces, modern services and high-tech foreign trade are steadily taking root," said Zhu Qigui, associate director of the China Academy of Financial Research.
"As long as China continues to rely on innovation, reform and its vast market, the trend of moving toward new and better development will not change," the scholar said.
A drone photo shows new energy vehicles to be exported at Yantai Port in east China's Shandong Province, Sept. 15, 2026. (Photo by Tang Ke/Xinhua)
SHARED OPPORTUNITIES
A major trading partner of as many as 169 countries and regions, China saw its goods trade rise 18.8 percent year on year to 39.94 trillion yuan in the first three quarters. In September alone, trade grew 27.5 percent.
In the first nine months, exports of mechanical and electrical products climbed 23.7 percent and accounted for 64.3 percent of total exports, while intermediate goods made up more than half of all exports, reinforcing China's role as a stabilizing anchor for global industrial and supply chains.
In east China's Anhui Province, robotics manufacturer EFORT Intelligent Robot Co., Ltd. has continued to see growth in overseas orders this year, with a batch of its spraying robots set to be exported to Italy. The company's overseas revenue increased by more than 50 percent year on year in the first half of 2026.
Meanwhile, the company's client, German automobile giant Volkswagen, is shifting its strategy from "in China, for China" to "in China, beyond China," with cars produced in China already exported to the Middle East and Central Asia.
Foreign-invested enterprises in China remained active players in the January-September period, with their imports and exports rising 19 percent to 11.69 trillion yuan, a record high for the same period. Their trade in intermediate goods grew 27.4 percent to 7.9 trillion yuan, and their high-tech product exports jumped 42.1 percent.
More foreign firms are embracing "China Opportunity 2.0," deepening their integration into China's industrial and innovation chains, Mao said.

item.title: Xi congratulates Central Institute of Socialism on 70th founding anniversary
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday sent a congratulatory letter to the Central Institute of Socialism, celebrating its 70th founding anniversary.
In the letter, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, praised the institute for training a large number of non-CPC representatives who share the CPC's ideals and work in unity toward common goals, and for making important contributions to consolidating and developing the patriotic united front over the past 70 years.
He encouraged the institute to continue strengthening political training, building broad political consensus, and improving the quality of its teaching and research as well as its governance capacity.
Xi called on the institute to play a greater role in training talent for the united front, conducting theoretical research and promoting principles and policies, so as to better serve the overall work of the CPC and the country.
The congratulatory letter was read out at a gathering marking the institute's anniversary in Beijing on Tuesday.
Wang Huning, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, addressed the event.
Wang said Xi's congratulatory message fully recognized the institute's achievements and contributions, and set out directions and requirements for strengthening the institute and enhancing its role.
Wang said the CPC Central Committee has consistently supported the development of the institute over the past 70 years. He called for stronger political consensus-building through sustained political training, higher-quality education to better train personnel for the united front, and continued efforts to enforce strict management of the institute.
The institute was established on Oct. 15, 1956. Over the past seven decades, it has made significant contributions to upholding and improving the system of multiparty cooperation under the leadership of the CPC and to consolidating and strengthening the patriotic united front.
Wang Huning, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, addresses a gathering marking the 70th founding anniversary of the Central Institute of Socialism in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 20, 2026. Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, on Tuesday sent a congratulatory letter to the Central Institute of Socialism, celebrating its 70th founding anniversary. The congratulatory letter was read out at the gathering marking the institute's anniversary in Beijing. (Xinhua/Liu Bin)

item.title: China railway passenger trips hit record high in first three quarters
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
Passengers are seen at Harbin Railway Station in Harbin, northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, Oct. 7, 2026. (Photo by Yuan Yong/Xinhua)
BEIJING, Oct. 18 (Xinhua) -- China's railway network handled 3.71 billion passenger trips in the first three quarters of 2026, up 4.8 percent year on year, the highest for the period, according to the China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. (China Railway).
During the period, the railway network operated an average of 11,511 passenger trains daily, up 5.3 percent from a year earlier.
Railway departments have actively responded to demand for sightseeing, wellness tours and red-themed study tours, according to China Railway. In the first nine months, a total of 2,860 tourist trains were operated across the country, up 25.5 percent year on year.
The railway network also operated 947 special trains for concertgoers and sports fans during the period, effectively boosting the catering, hotel and cultural tourism sectors.
Cross-border rail travel also continued to grow. The China-Laos Railway carried 265,000 cross-border trips, up 37.8 percent, while the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong high-speed railway handled over 25.8 million cross-border trips, up 11.8 percent, China Railway said.
China Railway also adapted to the inbound travel boom created by the country's visa-free transit policy. The railway network carried over 19 million foreign passenger trips in the first three quarters, up 33.4 percent year on year, the company said.
Behind the steady growth in passenger traffic is China's increasingly dense high-speed rail network.
By the end of 2025, the country's total operating railway mileage had reached 165,000 km, which included more than 50,000 km of high-speed rail.
On Sept. 28, China opened four high-speed rail sections, connecting Xiongan in north China's Hebei Province with Shangqiu in Henan Province in central China, Xi'an with Ankang in Shaanxi Province in northwest China, Yichang with Xingshan in central China's Hubei Province, and Harbin with Yichun in Heilongjiang Province in the country's northeast.
China's high-speed rail network is projected to hit 70,000 km by 2035, featuring eight north-south vertical lines and eight east-west horizontal lines. Once complete, the network will connect major cities, city clusters and key economic zones across the country.

item.title: The Long March: Half a Quilt
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
In November 1934, three female Red Army soldiers sheltered at villager Xu Jiexiu's home during the Long March. Seeing the impoverished family shivering without bedding, the soldiers cut their only marching quilt in half before departing: "When the revolution is won, we will bring you a new quilt."
Xu waited for 50 years. The elderly woman later said: "What is the Communist Party? They are the people who, even with just one quilt, will cut half of it off for the people."
Torn in two was a quilt; woven forever were the hearts of the people.

item.title: How can Ningxia wine make a lasting impression on the world?
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
"We don't need to be like everybody else." At the 47th World Congress of Vine and Wine in Yinchuan, Ningxia, the OIV President highlighted the unique stories that China and Ningxia have to tell.
From the achievements of a young wine region to the terroir between the Helan Mountains and the Yellow River—and a memorable glass of Marselan—international guests shared what stood out to them about Ningxia. Their reflections point to a way forward: build on the region's strengths and let the world discover its distinctive wines.
